title: LanternData carries lit_in, the light act records it, recall reports it and the fork reads the typed field
purpose: A fork has to know the session a lantern was lit in, because a copied line keeps its id and a fork's child holds a copy of every lantern on the copied chain. HOME-006 reads that session from a lit_in key the light act does not write, pulled from the entry's raw data as a stopgap, with fixtures writing the lit_in lantern by hand. This brief makes lit_in part of the lantern's typed shape: LanternData carries it, the light act records it, recall reports it, and the fork reads the typed field, while every lantern lit before it stays readable and forkable (ADR-029).
task:
Add an optional `lit_in` to `LanternData` in `crates/lys-home/src/record/entries.rs`, modelled so that an absent key, a present JSON null and a present non-string value stay three distinct things. `light()` writes `lit_in` as the id of the session it appends the lantern to, at that session's head, and its `Lit` report (printed by `lys-home lantern light`) carries `lit_in` beside `id`, `session`, `point` and `lit_at`. Recall's `LanternRow` carries `lit_in` beside `point`, `note` and `lit_by`, as JSON null for a lantern whose data has no `lit_in`. `fork_cut.rs` reads `point` and `lit_in` through a typed view instead of raw `serde_json::Value` lookups, keeping every behaviour it has today. The fork's fixtures light `L2` with the light act. In scope: `entries.rs`, `lantern.rs`, `recall.rs`, `fork_cut.rs`, their tests, `tests/lantern_cli.rs`, `tests/fork.rs`, `RECORD.md`, the lys-home README, a note in `PROOF-FORK.md`, and the cluster's rendered markdown.

A correction to the request, as the lead ruled: the request states that a lantern with no lit_in is refused by name as the tree does now, and the tree does not refuse it. A lantern whose data has no `lit_in` key is an older record and resolves by its holders as ADR-017 and HOME-006's third amendment rule: one holder cuts, several give `lantern_ambiguous` until `--session` names one. Only a `lit_in` that is present and not a session id is refused by name (`lit_in_not_a_session`), never read as any session. ADR-017 is not retired, and every lantern lit before this brief stays forkable. `lit_in` is optional: a lantern lit before this brief is read as it is, never as the wrong shape; recall by note skips no session it lists today for want of `lit_in`, and recall by point refuses nothing new for want of it.

The fixtures, as the lead ruled: the rule against hand-written lantern entries in the fork's fixtures covers every lantern the light act can produce, so `L2` is lit with the light act in both fork fixtures. The records the light act can no longer write stay hand-written: the older records `O2` (in both fixtures), `M2` and `N3` with no `lit_in`, the copy `N2` whose `lit_in` names another session, and `N1` to `N4` with `lit_in` null, 5, `../elsewhere` and `no-such-session`. Each is marked in its test as standing for a record the light act cannot produce. Because the light act chooses the lantern's id, a test that named `L2` by its literal id compares with the id the light act returned (`lanterns.l2`); no assertion, count or refusal changes otherwise.

The two key-set pins are updated, as the lead ruled: `lantern_data_round_trips_with_exactly_its_four_keys` becomes `lantern_data_round_trips_with_exactly_its_five_keys` with `lit_in`, and `a_row_carries_exactly_its_fields` gains `lit_in`. The light report's pin in `tests/lantern_cli.rs` gains `lit_in`. No other existing lantern or fork test changes beyond the literal-id replacement above.

Recall's refusal, as the lead ruled: a lantern whose `lit_in` is present and not a session id is refused in recall as `lit_in_not_a_session`, with the fork's four reason texts, both as the skip reason by note and as the refusal by point, and is never listed as a row. Recall's other `entry_shape` cases keep their name.

Out of scope: re-measuring PROOF-FORK on a real session whose lanterns carry lit_in; recall telling a lantern lit in a session from a copy a fork carried in; and retiring the older-record holder rule. The card is ordered after HOME-006, which is on main, so it starts on the current main.

requirements.title: Give LanternData an optional lit_in that keeps null and non-string values distinct from an absent key
requirements.spec: Structural. `LanternData` in `record/entries.rs` gains a documented fifth field `lit_in: Option<LitIn>`: the session that held the point when the lantern was lit. `LitIn` is a public enum declared beside it, `#[serde(untagged)]`, with `LitIn::Session(String)` for a JSON string and `LitIn::Other(serde_json::Value)` for any other JSON value, null included, each documented. The field carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none", deserialize_with = ...)]` naming a crate function that wraps whatever value is present in `Some`, so an absent key reads as `None` and a present `null` reads as `Some(LitIn::Other(Value::Null))`. `LanternData` keeps `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, and `EpilogueData` does not change. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT read a present null as an absent key, SHALL NOT make `lit_in` required, SHALL NOT refuse a lantern whose data has no `lit_in`, and SHALL NOT rename or retype `point`, `note`, `lit_by` or `lit_at`.
acceptance: `serde_json::from_value::<LanternData>(json!({"point": "e2", "note": NOTE, "lit_by": LIGHTER, "lit_at": now()}))` is `Ok` with `lit_in == None`.
The same object with `"lit_in": null` added is `Ok` with `lit_in == Some(LitIn::Other(Value::Null))`.
The same object with `"lit_in": 5` added is `Ok` with `lit_in == Some(LitIn::Other(json!(5)))`.
The same object with `"lit_in": "parent"` added is `Ok` with `lit_in == Some(LitIn::Session("parent".to_owned()))`.

`lantern_data_round_trips_with_exactly_its_five_keys` builds a `LanternData` with `lit_in: Some(LitIn::Session(..))`, and its sorted serialised keys equal `["lit_at", "lit_by", "lit_in", "note", "point"]` and it deserialises back equal; no test named `lantern_data_round_trips_with_exactly_its_four_keys` remains.
A `LanternData` with `lit_in: None` serialises to exactly the keys `["lit_at", "lit_by", "note", "point"]`.
`lantern_data_with_an_extra_key_is_refused` passes unchanged: data carrying `"anchors": []` is `Err`.
`git diff` of `record/entries.rs` changes no line of `EpilogueData`.

requirements.title: Record lit_in in the light act and print it in the light report
requirements.spec: WHEN `light(home, session, point, note, by)` appends a lantern, THE SYSTEM SHALL write its data's `lit_in` as `Some(LitIn::Session(session))`, the id of the session at whose head the lantern is appended, and SHALL return a `Lit` report carrying a documented `lit_in: String` field equal to that id beside `id`, `session`, `point` and `lit_at`; `lys-home lantern light` prints that report. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT take `lit_in` from an argument, from the point entry, or from any other session, SHALL NOT change the order of `light`'s checks or its refusals, and SHALL NOT put the note in the report.
acceptance: In `lantern_tests.rs`, `light(&home, FIXTURE, "e2", NOTE, LIGHTER)` returns a `Lit` whose `lit_in == FIXTURE`, and the appended entry's data read as `LanternData` has `lit_in == Some(LitIn::Session(FIXTURE.to_owned()))`.

In `tests/lantern_cli.rs`, the light report's sorted keys equal `["id", "lit_at", "lit_in", "point", "session"]` and `report["lit_in"] == FIXTURE`; the existing assertion that stdout does not contain `NOTE` still holds.
Every other test in `lantern_tests.rs` and `tests/lantern_cli.rs` passes unchanged.

requirements.title: Read lit_in in the fork from the typed field, keeping the holder rule and the named refusals
requirements.spec: `read_lantern` in `record/fork_cut.rs` deserialises the lantern entry's data into a crate-private view holding `point: String` and a `lit_in` declared with R1's `LitIn` type and R1's deserialiser; the view does not deny unknown keys and does not require `note`, `lit_by` or `lit_at`, so every lantern the fork resolves today still resolves. The check of a present `lit_in` is one `pub(crate)` function in `fork_cut.rs` taking the home, the lantern id and the `Option<&LitIn>` and returning the session id or the refusal. IF the data has no `lit_in` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve by the holders exactly as today: one holder cuts, several refuse `lantern_ambiguous` until a session is named. IF `lit_in` is present and is null, not a string, not a safe session name, or names no session of the home THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse `lit_in_not_a_session` with `what` equal to `is null`, `is not a string`, `is not a safe session name` and `names no session of the home` respectively. IF the data does not deserialise into the view (no `point`, or a `point` that is not a string) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse `EntryShape` as today. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT look up a `lit_in` key in a raw `serde_json::Value`, SHALL NOT read a present `lit_in` that is not a session id as any session, SHALL NOT refuse a lantern for having no `lit_in`, and SHALL NOT change the names or display prefixes of `lit_in_not_a_session`, `lantern_not_lit_here` and `lantern_ambiguous`, the cut, the copied line bytes, the ancestry entries or the fork report.
acceptance: `grep -c '"lit_in"' crates/lys-home/src/record/fork_cut.rs` prints `0`.

`a_lit_in_that_is_not_a_session_id_is_refused_by_name` passes with `refusals == 8`: `N1` gives `is null`, `N2` `is not a string`, `N3` `is not a safe session name` and `N4` `names no session of the home`, each with no session named and with `A` named, each display text starting `lit_in_not_a_session`.
`a_lit_in_session_that_holds_no_copy_refuses_naming_the_holder_read` passes with `refusals == 3`, each `LanternNotLitHere` with `lit_in == "elsewhere"`.

In `a_lit_in_lantern_cuts_from_its_session_and_an_older_record_needs_one_named`, `O2` (no `lit_in`) with no session named refuses `LanternAmbiguous` with `sessions == ["A", PARENT]`, and with `PARENT` named cuts `["e1", "e2"]` with `lit_in == None`.

`fork(&home, "M2", None)` still reports `(entries, blocks, unstored) == (2, 1, 2)`, and every test in `fork_tests.rs` that forks `N3` passes unchanged, though neither lantern's data carries `lit_at` or `lit_in`.

`HomeError::LitInNotASession`, `HomeError::LanternNotLitHere` and `HomeError::LanternAmbiguous` and their `#[error]` texts are unchanged in `git diff` of `crates/lys-home/src/error.rs`, which is empty.

requirements.title: Report lit_in in recall's rows, null for a lantern without it
requirements.spec: `LanternRow` in `record/recall.rs` gains a documented `lit_in: Option<String>`, serialised without `skip_serializing_if`, so every row carries the key beside `point`, `note` and `lit_by`. WHEN recall by note or by point lists a lantern whose data has no `lit_in`, THE SYSTEM SHALL list it with `lit_in` null. WHEN it lists a lantern whose `lit_in` is present, THE SYSTEM SHALL check it by R3's rule and list the session id it names. IF that check refuses THEN the refusal SHALL be `lit_in_not_a_session` with R3's `what` text (`is null`, `is not a string`, `is not a safe session name` or `names no session of the home`): recall by note SHALL skip the lantern's session and name it in `skipped` with that refusal's display text, and recall by point SHALL return that refusal. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT give such a lantern `entry_shape`, SHALL NOT change the name of recall's other `entry_shape` refusals, SHALL NOT list a lantern whose `lit_in` is present and not a session id as a row, SHALL NOT skip or refuse a lantern for having no `lit_in`, and SHALL NOT print a line of the transcript (ADR-015).
acceptance: `a_row_carries_exactly_its_fields` asserts row keys `["epilogues", "id", "lit_at", "lit_by", "lit_in", "note", "point", "session"]`, and still counts 2 rows and 2 epilogues.

A lantern lit with `light(&home, OTHER, "o1", ..)` recalls by point `(OTHER, "o1")` as one row whose `lit_in == Some(OTHER.to_owned())`, and every row `recall_by_note(&home, "fold")` lists has `lit_in` equal to its own `session`.

A lantern appended with `Session::append_entry` whose data is exactly `{point, note, lit_by, lit_at}` recalls by its point as one row with `lit_in == None`, serialised as `"lit_in": null`, and `recall_by_note` on a phrase of its note lists it with `skipped` empty.

Four sessions each holding one lantern whose `lit_in` is null, 5, `"../elsewhere"` and `"no-such-session"`: `recall_by_note` on the lanterns' note lists those four sessions in `skipped` and no row from them, each skip's `reason` starting `lit_in_not_a_session` and containing `is null`, `is not a string`, `is not a safe session name` and `names no session of the home` respectively; `recall_by_point` at each lantern's point is `Err(HomeError::LitInNotASession { .. })` with `what` equal to those four texts respectively; the test counts 4 skips and 4 refusals, and no skip reason starts `entry_shape`.
Every other test in `recall_tests.rs` passes unchanged.

requirements.title: Light L2 with the light act in both fork fixtures
requirements.spec: In `fixture_home` of `record/fork_cut_tests.rs`, `L2` is lit with `light(&home, PARENT, "e2", NOTE, LIGHTER)` while `parent`'s head is `e2` and no owner holds it, and in `fixture_home` of `tests/fork.rs` with `lys-home lantern light` at `--session parent --point e2`; `Lanterns.l2` holds the returned id and `O2` is appended as its child. The lanterns the fork fixtures write by hand are exactly those the light act cannot produce: `O2` in both fixtures, `M2` and `N3` in `fork_tests.rs` (no `lit_in`), `N2` (a `lit_in` naming a session other than the one it stands in) and `N1` to `N4` (`lit_in` null, 5, `../elsewhere`, `no-such-session`) in `fork_cut_tests.rs`, each call site carrying a comment that it stands for a record the light act cannot produce. A test that named `L2` by its literal id compares with `lanterns.l2`. The module doc of `tests/fork.rs` says `L2` is lit with `lys-home lantern light`. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write by hand any lantern the light act can produce, SHALL NOT drop or weaken a hand-written refusal or older-record case, and SHALL NOT change any assertion, count or refusal beyond the literal-id replacement.
acceptance: `grep -c '"L2"'` prints `0` for `crates/lys-home/src/record/fork_cut_tests.rs`, `crates/lys-home/src/record/fork_tests.rs` and `crates/lys-home/tests/fork.rs`.

`grep -c 'lantern_entry('` prints `4` for `fork_cut_tests.rs` (the helper and the `O2`, `N2` and `N1` to `N4` sites), `2` for `fork_tests.rs` (`M2`, `N3`) and `2` for `tests/fork.rs` (the helper and `O2`).
`grep -c 'the light act cannot produce'` prints `3` for `fork_cut_tests.rs`, `2` for `fork_tests.rs` and `1` for `tests/fork.rs`.

`five_forks_succeed_and_five_are_refused_with_the_ancestry_on_the_parent` passes with 5 children, 5 refusals and 5 `lys.fork` marks, the `lantern_not_lit_here` refusal still coming from `L2` named with a session it was not lit in.
`cargo test -p lys-home --all-features` passes with the count of `#[test]` functions in `fork_cut_tests.rs`, `fork_tests.rs` and `tests/fork.rs` unchanged from the base commit.

requirements.title: Document lit_in in the record, the README and the fork proof, and render the cluster
requirements.spec: Structural. `docs/design/home/RECORD.md`'s `lys.lantern` bullet lists `{point, note, lit_by, lit_at, lit_in}` and states that `lit_in` is the id of the session the light act appended the lantern to, absent from a lantern lit before HOME-010; its Forks section states that a lantern with no `lit_in` resolves by its holders and a present `lit_in` that is not a session id is refused `lit_in_not_a_session`. The `lys.lantern` row of the lys-home README's custom-entry table lists `lit_in`. `docs/design/home/PROOF-FORK.md` keeps its measured sentence that the light act on the measured tree records no `lit_in` byte for byte, and gains a note directly after it that from HOME-010 the light act records `lit_in`, and that lanterns lit before it, as those measured, resolve by the older-record rule. `HOME-010.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `CHECKLIST.md` and `USER-STORIES.md` are rendered from their JSON with `scripts/design/render-brief.py` and `scripts/design/render-cluster.py`. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT rewrite any measured figure, hash, command or result in PROOF-FORK.md, and SHALL NOT edit any rendered markdown by hand.
acceptance: `grep -c 'point, note, lit_by, lit_at, lit_in' docs/design/home/RECORD.md` prints `1`.
`grep -c 'lit_in_not_a_session' docs/design/home/RECORD.md` prints at least `1`.
The README line beginning `| \`lys.lantern\`` contains `lit_in`.
`git diff` of `docs/design/home/PROOF-FORK.md` deletes no line, and the added lines contain `HOME-010` and `lit_in`.
`sh scripts/design/gate.sh` exits 0.

boundaries: SHALL NOT rewrite, truncate or delete any byte of an existing session line; a lantern lit before this brief stays as it is (P1, ADR-014).
SHALL NOT refuse, skip or read as the wrong shape a lantern whose data has no lit_in, and SHALL NOT retire ADR-017's older-record rule.
SHALL NOT change the names or display prefixes of lit_in_not_a_session, lantern_not_lit_here or lantern_ambiguous, and SHALL NOT change error.rs.
SHALL NOT change the fork's cut, its copied line bytes, its ancestry entries or its report fields.
SHALL NOT change EpilogueData, and SHALL NOT remove deny_unknown_fields from LanternData.
SHALL NOT change the Claude Code render or its derived uuids (ADR-016), and SHALL NOT render a lantern into a resume file (C30).
SHALL NOT put a note, epilogue words or any transcript content in a refusal, a report, a log line, a test name or a proof document; only recall prints notes and epilogues (ADR-015).
SHALL NOT mark or filter in recall a lantern copied into a fork's child, and SHALL NOT re-measure PROOF-FORK on a real session.
SHALL NOT add a file beyond HOME-010.md.
